newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 10.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* NASD President Frank Zarb is reviewing consolidating the boards of Nasdaq market and NASD's regulatory arm because it is too unwieldly.
* Sherwood Securities was the first Nasdaq dealer to seek settlement under a closely-followed suit, agreeing to pay $9.2 million to resolve civil allegations about trading practices.
* General Electric and Dow Chemical resolved litigation in which Dow alleged General Electric hired Dow employees who were privy to trade secrets.
* Ford management is seen recommending the board boost the company's quarterly dividend by 12 percent to $0.43, according to people familiar with the matter.
* Procter & Gamble's plan to buy Tambrands for $50 per share will likely draw regulatory scrutiny.
* Nippon Credit Bank and Bankers Trust agreed to form a business alliance in which Bankers Trust would take over $18 billion of Nippon's overseas assets.
* Three analysts downgraded Merck shares on concerns a new cholesterol-lowering statin drug posed a threat to Merck's Zocor and shares fell.
* A U.S. textile industry group accused the Limited of buying Chinese-made garments and claiming they were products of Hong Kong.
* The CEO of Citicorp said the bank could face prosecution for its role in alleged money laundering by Raul Salinas, the brother of former Mexican President Carlos Salinas de Gortari.
* A BankAmerica class-action settlement plan related to its mortgage financing unit has been criticized for giving more money to the lawyers instead of the plaintiffs.
* The Dow Jones industrials fell 45.32 to 6563.84.
* Tenet and MedPartners said they would form a health-care network in Southern California which included 33 hospitals and over 4,000 doctors.
* Tele-Communications Inc said it would not spin off three of its units because the IRS declined to rule on whether the deal would be tax-free to shareholders.
* Heard on the Street: Investors with weak hearts might benefit from some of Merck's drugs but investors with strong stomachs may want to take a look at its stock.
* Credit markets: Bonds ended little changed, as investors and traders waited for reports today and tomorow that will shed light on the strength of consumer spending.
